articles.title: Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers becoming one of Premier League's most dangerous double acts - The Radar
articles.summary: Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers combined to deadly effect for Chelsea against Leeds; The Radar column looks at how their on-pitch relationship is flourishing under Xabi Alonso; Alex Scott's strong start to the season for Bournemouth also features
articles.body:
Welcome to The Radar , a Sky Sports column in which Nick Wright uses a blend of data and opinion to shed light on need-to-know Premier League stories. This week:

🔺 Palmer-Rogers double act analysed 🔺 Scott starring for Bournemouth 🔺 Crystal Palace's tough-tackler

Morgan Rogers was bemused when he found out Cole Palmer was man of the match in Chelsea's win over Leeds. "I got four assists," he pleaded. "I'll say you should have had it," replied a smiling Palmer. "Don't mention me. I'm just a bystander," added Rogers.

The exchange, captured by the Sky Sports cameras before their post-match interview, showed the chemistry between the pair. It can be seen on the pitch too. Do they feel like they've been playing together forever? "We pretty much have," answered Rogers.

Close friends and former team-mates in England and Manchester City's youth teams, Rogers and Palmer have picked up where they left off at Chelsea, wreaking havoc either side of Joao Pedro and providing a combined 11 goals and assists in five games so far. Only Arsenal have managed to keep them relatively quiet.

Their half-time introductions inspired Chelsea's comeback on Wednesday. After Rogers had ingeniously flicked the ball off his backside to set up Palmer's equaliser, the pair could be seen combining in the lead-up to Chelsea's third and sixth goals too.

Those combinations have become a theme. Across Chelsea's five games so far, Rogers has played nearly twice as many passes to Palmer as any other player, with 19, while only defender Josh Acheampong has received more passes from Palmer, on 15.

They have only directly combined for one goal, surprisingly. But that total could easily be higher. In the 4-3 win over Brighton, they took it in turns to tee each other up, only to be denied by last-ditch blocks. In their opener against Fulham, Rogers created three shooting chances for Palmer but he couldn't capitalise.

In total, they have created nine chances for each other, which is more than twice as many as any other two players in the Premier League, ahead of five pairings, among them Palmer and Joao Pedro and Antoine Semenyo and Erling Haaland, on four.

Although most expected Palmer to be the provider for Rogers, it has more commonly been the other way around so far. Palmer finished last season with a run of one goal in 13 games but has four in five this term, his threat increased thanks in part to his new team-mate.

Rogers explained how they intended to help each other after his arrival. "We have different qualities, different ways of playing and affecting games," he said. "Ultimately, it's about scoring and creating and linking the game. We can do that in our own ways."

The differences can be seen in how they feed each other. Rogers typically aims to find Palmer in space between the opponent's defensive and midfield lines, as in the examples below.

Rogers is similarly adept at finding space between the lines. But he also offers a threat in behind, something Palmer has attempted to exploit with passes targeting his forward runs.

It helps that in Xabi Alonso's system, the width is provided by the wing-backs. This gives Rogers and Palmer freedom to come inside, putting them in close proximity to each other and giving them more opportunities to combine in central areas.

With Rogers and Palmer playing off each other centrally, Chelsea have directed a higher percentage of attacks through the middle third of the pitch than any other Premier League side.

Hull, visitors to Stamford Bridge on Saturday, are the next side tasked with stopping them. Recent evidence suggests their run of three straight clean sheets may be at risk.

While Chelsea were able to strengthen their attack with the signing of Rogers, their efforts to bolster their midfield were less successful. One of the players who got away from them in the summer continues to go from strength to strength at Bournemouth.

Alex Scott was valued highly by Andoni Iraola and the same is true for Marco Rose. "I love him," he said after their 2-2 draw with Newcastle last weekend. It was the third game in a row in which they have lost a lead late on and it felt particularly harsh on Scott.

The 23-year-old, scorer of Bournemouth's opener in their previous game against Everton, was the best player on the pitch at St James' Park. In addition to having a hand in both Bournemouth goals, he had more touches, made more final-third passes and contested more duels than any of his team-mates.

It was a continuation of a strong start to the season. Scott has showcased his blend of physical and technical qualities, working tirelessly and eating up ground as he shuttles between both boxes. There is a sense that he is taking more responsibility too.

It all bodes well for his future. Carry on like this and the clubs who coveted him during the summer will likely return in January. But for now Bournemouth will just hope for more of the same from him when they face Brentford at the Vitality Stadium on Saturday.

Anan Khalaili has big shoes to fill at Crystal Palace having replaced Daniel Munoz in the right wing-back position. He provided evidence of his attacking threat with the driving run to set up Ben Chilwell's winning goal against Fulham last weekend.

But it's at the other end that he's been busiest. Khalaili has had some awkward moments defensively but he clearly relishes his one-vs-one battles and he has come out on top more often than not.

In fact, in addition to winning the second-most duels in the division so far, the 21-year-old, a summer signing from Union Saint-Gilloise, ranks top for tackles. His total of 17 puts him five clear of any other player. It's some going given he has only started twice.

Player Radar: Who else to keep an eye on

Igor Thiago faces Bournemouth on Saturday aiming to get off the mark this season. The Brentford striker has registered 2.30 expected goals without scoring in the opening three games, the highest total of any player yet to find the net. Time for his luck to change?

Four Premier League games will be shown live on Sky Sports this weekend, starting with Tottenham vs Everton on Saturday evening.

Sunday's action sees Coventry host Brighton at 2pm, followed by the Manchester derby as Man Utd face Man City at 4.30pm.

The weekend's live coverage concludes with Monday Night Football , when Leeds host Newcastle in the 8pm kick-off, with coverage starting at 6.30pm.

Arsenal's ever-improving defence was the focus of the last column ahead of their meeting with Morgan Rogers and Chelsea .

articles.title: Liverpool fail Fulham test as Chelsea's defensive problems continue to hamper their title challenge credentials - Premier League hits and misses
articles.summary: The Sky Sports football writers analyse Saturday's Premier League action as Liverpool fail to inspire in goalless draw with Fulham; Chelsea held by newly-promoted Hull in further showing of defensive frailties; Aston Villa have major attacking concerns
articles.body:
Much of the talk surrounding the Chelsea team that Xabi Alonso is in the midst of creating is what they are capable of in attack. How can you stop JP Morgan?

No one has been able to stop them from contributing at least one goal per game this season, but you can't bank on them to get you out of footballing bankruptcy if you can't keep clean sheets.

It is a problem that has impacted the Blues for some time, not just under Alonso. This is the 20th Premier League game in a row their defence has been breached.

The signing of a World Cup winner and multi-time Yashin trophy winner in the form of Emi Martinez is all well and good. However, if he has defenders not doing the basics in front of him, he may as well be Robert Sanchez.

The 1.32 xG that Hull managed was a fair reflection of how dangerous they were at times at Stamford Bridge. And it wasn't like they carved open the hosts. Most of the time, they had chances put on a plate.

The potential in attack is obvious, and certainly exciting. However, Alonso needs to tap into his learnings under Jose Mourinho and make this Chelsea side much tougher to score against if he wants to challenge. Callum Bishop

There were celebrations at Anfield on Wednesday when Andoni Iraola picked up the first Champions League win of his coaching career against Atletico Madrid. But that win was always going to come at some point this season. There was a bigger question.

One of the themes of this Liverpool season was always likely to be how the new coach would be able to cope with an increased schedule, having impressed at Rayo Vallecano and Bournemouth without the added challenge of European commitments.

As it happened | Teams | Stats | Watch FREE PL highlights

Latest news and rumours: Liverpool | Fulham

This was the first test of that and Liverpool did not pass it. They were unable to play at the tempo that Iraola usually demands, starting slowly and struggling to raise the level. Fulham were well worth their first point of the campaign and looked as likely to win it.

Iraola's unbeaten run as Liverpool boss continues, one that extends back to the first week of January for him personally given his exploits with the Cherries. But home games against Nottingham Forest and Fulham have yielded only two points. More is needed.

Asked in the press conference whether the fatigue explained Liverpool's performance, Iraola replied: "In the end, this is the easier one, for me, for you, for everyone - our players were tired. I think there is a lack of freshness, definitely. We cannot hide it.

"I think it's the worst turnaround in terms of 60-something hours between the games, after a very big game the other day. But this is going to happen more times, maybe with one more day, maybe."

The onus is going to be on Iraola to find the answers. Adam Bate

Bruno Guimaraes didn't hesitate when asked after Arsenal's 2-0 win over Sunderland whether he sees David Raya as the best goalkeeper in the world. "Definitely," he said.

The midfielder's sensational goal completed a remarkable two-minute turnaround at the Stadium of Light but it was Raya's brilliant penalty save from Enzo Le Fee that made it possible.

Arteta was adamant the spot kick should never have been awarded. But Raya's sole focus was to stop it from going in. Le Fee, who scored a penalty last weekend, struck it well. Raya, though, showed his athleticism, diving low to his left to make the save.

It was a brilliant piece of goalkeeping and there were plenty of other examples over the course of the 90 minutes. Sunderland are about as physical as opponents come but Raya dominated his penalty box, claiming crosses and exuding calm.

His late save to deny Nordi Mukiele, following a fabulous centre by Granit Xhaka, when Arsenal were still only a goal up, was another crucial intervention. And he was straight back up on his feet to scramble away the follow-up. Raya is always alert to danger.

He had to settle for a place on the bench with Spain at the World Cup. But there can be little doubting his status as the Premier League's best, if not the world's, and his value to his team-mates and manager is abundantly clear.

He was Arsenal's difference-maker - and not for the first time. Nick Wright

It doesn't take a genius to figure out where Tottenham's biggest concern lies right now. You can't win games if you don't score goals. That's why Spurs haven't won a league game this season, after going 400 minutes without finding the net.

They have so many creative players, all of whom were on the pitch against the Toffees. Yet the man who they need to score the bulk of their goals was anonymous. Or at the very least, wasn't found.

Latest news and rumours: Tottenham | Everton

Dominic Solanke's fitness for Tottenham feels imperative. As the only out and out number nine available to De Zerbi, the Englishman has to be picked when fit. Purely because it seems Spurs don't have a choice.

However, whether it be rustiness following his latest setbacks or another reason, Solanke didn't offer anywhere near enough as the number nine. He managed just 19 touches. That's less than Kinsky in goal.

More worryingly, he had zero shots. If the man whose job is to find the net isn't even letting fly at it, no wonder Spurs are struggling in the final third.

Only De Zerbi can answer if the reason for this is because his team-mates aren't utlising him enough, or if Solanke can't be relied upon to be the replacement to Harry Kane. Of course, replacing Kane is practically impossible. But, in the three years since he left for Germany, Solanke is the only one Spurs have splashed the cash on to fill his shoes.

While reinforcements were clearly needed across the pitch after last season, the fact a fitter, more reliable striker wasn't on the agenda is a concern. And it's biting Spurs now. They can't get an improvement until January now, so De Zerbi has to find a way to get Solanke more involved. Callum Bishop

Bournemouth are now the first team to lead in each of their opening four Premier League games of a season and fail to win any of them.

Marco Rose said it was clear after their Newcastle draw that game management was something they needed to remedy. You can't help but feel a touch sympathetic for a side freely creating as they are.

Latest news and rumours: Bournemouth | Brentford

They took 20 shots with 10 being on target, while Brentford only tested Dorde Petrovic's goal twice. You'd expect two goals in the game off those statistics alone.

The concern will be the speed at which they allowed Brentford back in though.

Against Brentford, they went 2-1 up and conceded again within three minutes. Brentford didn't have to wait long to find a way back into the game, and that's becoming the recurring theme for Bournemouth.

There's clearly enough in this team to win football matches. But until they can control those periods after scoring, and prevent opponents from immediately regaining momentum, they're going to keep leaving points on the table.

Four games, four leads, no wins. Welcome to the Premier League, Marco Rose. William Bitibiri

When they first returned to the Premier League in 2024/25, it was 16 games before Ipswich had recorded two wins.

This time around, it has taken just four.

They beat Sunderland on the opening day, took the lead against Man Utd at Old Trafford the following week - before an eventual 5-2 defeat - and recorded a higher xG than Liverpool in the 2-0 loss last time out.

And against Crystal Palace, both Emersonn and Leif Davis' headers were all too easy. Axel Disasi's sending off gave them an extra boost, but they took advantage when opportunities presented themselves.

When Palace's equaliser made it 2-2, they did not go all out, desperate for the winner; they just waited, exercising patience, with the belief the winner would come, which it eventually did.

While taking three points at Selhurst Park was impressive, equally - if not more so - was the fact it was the third time in the four games they have played that they have conceded less than 0.70 xG.

Fellow newly-promoted side Hull are taking all the plaudits for their start on their return to the Premier League, and rightly so - but, out of the spotlight, Ipswich are going well, too. Dan Long

Aston Villa managed just seven shots against Nottingham Forest. That is the third-lowest shot count they have posted in 59 home league games under Unai Emery.

It wasn't just that Villa failed to score more than once. It was the manner of their attacking play. Everything looked difficult. There was a lack of fluency, a lack of penetration and a lack of ideas.

Villa have undergone significant change this summer and it takes time for new players to understand each other's movements, particularly in the final third. There is also a new goalkeeper behind them and fresh faces still adapting to Emery's demands.

Seven shots at home is a red flag though, regardless of the personnel.

Villa need to find ways of getting their attacking players into dangerous positions more frequently. The worrying thing is that Forest didn't need to produce a defensive masterclass to restrict them.

Of course, Unai Emery is one of the best coaches around at solving problems. He will know this is one that needs addressing quickly. Lewis Jones

The one who bullied defenders at Ipswich. The one who made centre-backs uncomfortable simply by running towards them. The one who plays football like a battering ram.

There was something wonderfully uncomplicated about his performance in Nottingham Forest's 2-1 victory at Aston Villa.

Delap ran the channels relentlessly, chased lost causes and gave Villa's defenders absolutely no time to settle. He was aggressive without being reckless and looked like he was enjoying himself.

He took aim and unleashed a strike that flew into the net with the sort of power that summed up his afternoon perfectly.

That is what Forest signed him for. Lewis Jones

articles.title: Max Dowman: Arsenal prodigy delivers latest statement performance as Mikel Arteta urges caution over 16-year-old
articles.summary: Max Dowman scored twice for Arsenal in their 4-2 win at Ipswich Town in the Carabao Cup third round; the 16-year-old forward was making his first appearance of the season; Dowman has had to wait for his chance after becoming the Premier League's youngest scorer
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has managed the prodigy carefully since his big moment last season, when he became the Premier League's youngest scorer in a vital 2-0 home win over Everton on their title charge.

Dowman has played six times since then, mostly in cameos, and has been an unused substitute on four occasions this season. Last Saturday, he played an hour for the U21s in their 4-1 defeat to Chelsea while the first team won at Sunderland. Arteta warned Dowman afterwards that he must earn his minutes this season.

But Dowman did not have to wait long for his chance. While £63.5m striker Viktor Gyokeres failed to take his opportunity during Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night , Dowman excelled, and the ease with which he scored twice was frightening.

His first, in just the seventh minute, came after he stole possession in midfield, burst onto the ball before Gyokeres, shimmyed past Cedric Kipre to leave the defender on the ground, before sending goalkeeper Christian Walton the wrong way with his weaker right foot.

"That's something very natural for him," said Arteta. "He can deliver those actions effortlessly. I would say that's his biggest quality."

Dowman had to be more precise for his second. Martin Zubimendi's pass deflected off Jacob Greaves's left arm, and Dowman, with little space inside the penalty area, adjusted to the ricochet with two quick touches to set up an accurate, composed shot on his left foot that almost trickled over the line, such was the perfectly measured weight of the effort.

Dowman's performance will only increase the hype around him. How will Arteta manage that?

"Well, it depends. If he does what he does on the pitch, it's not easy, I understand," said Arteta. "But what we have to do is look after him. He's 16 years old. You don't see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that's a totally different context.

"But in this league, with the demands that the league [has], the players and everything put on you, we really need to make sure every time we throw him in, he's in the right context with the right preparation. That's what we are trying to do."

It wasn't all about the goals at Portman Road. Dowman, who only completed his GCSEs in August, also showed his work rate off the ball, pressing Ipswich into a mistake for Noni Madueke's goal.

"Defensively, his application, his capacity as well to sustain the actions, is not easy," added Arteta.

"He's 16 years old, and he can create moments, but to consistently go through the game, every phase, with the demands that we put on them, to be able to do that is extremely difficult. And he's coping better and better and better.

"He did the action where he regained the ball and won it. In the first goal, he loses his man. And that's the thing that we need to continue to reiterate with him because he's an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play at the biggest stage and still handle the situation with such naturality."

The evening wasn't even all about Dowman. Marli Salmon, 17, made only his second start for the first team and impressed at centre-back with an assured performance.

"Just having two 16-year-olds playing for Arsenal at this level against a Premier League team is so fulfilling," said Arteta. "Because I've been there and just to be able to contribute in somebody's career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight is just phenomenal.

"Medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we're going to have two tremendous footballers for the future."

Dowman has benefited from Arsenal's stability under Arteta. The club has been able to nurture and develop him, without the distraction of cycling through managers. On the same day 15-year-old JJ Gabriel asked to leave Manchester United , Dowman made his latest statement on the pitch.

Arsenal fans will be desperate to see more of him. Arteta has warned it's not so easy to play him regularly.

"Everything is possible. The probability [of playing regularly] is probably extremely low because you don't see the players with the capacity to handle just the physicality of the game," he said.

"Not only that, but the demands that you have to put your body through in the week to be able to be in good condition to compete, the amount of information, the challenges that you have to face. But he's doing it and he's doing it really well every time there's a chance."

Merson: Dowman is a generational talent but he needs to be patient

Sky Sports' Paul Merson on Dowman's future:

"I don't know what words you can use. The lad is just unbelievable. You've got to consider his age. He's going past players like they're not there, like he's playing in his own age group.

"The first goal on Tuesday, the way he throws the dummy, leaves the defender on his backside and scores. It's just unbelievable.

"He's at an unbelievable Rolls Royce of a football club. He's got 15 years at least at the top. He's just got to be patient and it's hard because he'll think that he should be playing in the team now.

"It's unbelievable what Arsenal have done and everyone involved there should be very proud of what they have produced and made him the player he is. I cannot talk highly enough about him.

"You've got to look after him. He's quite a big lad. I wouldn't worry about him getting bullied and kicked all over the place in the Premier League. There's VAR and that just doesn't happen any more in this day and age.

"I was disappointed at the Community Shield when Arsenal were 3-0 up. I was thinking, put him on now up against the creme de la creme and they didn't put him on and I just found that a bit strange.

"He'll be playing in the cup games, and hopefully it keeps on continuing because, as I say, these talented generational players come along once in a blue moon with Gazza [Paul Gascoigne], [Wayne] Rooney and now we're looking at Dowman."

articles.title: Max Dowman shines again for Arsenal and JJ Gabriel wants Man Utd exit, so which clubs have most valuable teens? Between the Lines
articles.summary: The Premier League's young sensations are making waves but which clubs have the most valuable teens? Between the Lines, the Sky Sports strand breaking down the data behind football's big stories, takes a look using Transfermarkt valuations
articles.body:
Dowman, 16, scored twice in Arsenal's Carabao Cup win over Ipswich, only hours after 15-year-old Gabriel had stunned Manchester United with his request to cancel his registration at the club.

Dowman's breakthrough and Gabriel's desire for first-team opportunities show how the stars of tomorrow are starting younger, but which Premier League clubs have the most valuable teens?

For this week's Between the Lines , we use Transfermarkt valuations to rank Premier League clubs by teenage value, albeit with the caveat that Transfermarkt does not assign valuations to young players with no first-team experience such as Gabriel.

According to Transfermarkt , Manchester City have the most valuable teenagers at a combined £122.6m, putting them just ahead of Chelsea on £121m, and Arsenal in third on £102.4m.

Brighton have the fourth-highest teenage value at £100.7m, reflecting their knack for identifying high-potential young signings in the transfer market, and putting them well ahead of fifth-placed Liverpool , who have a teenage value of £64.3m.

Manchester United set the standard for youth development in the Sir Alex Ferguson era but their teen value of £48.1m suggests they are no longer a top destination for young players and leaves them sixth, just ahead of Hull , who punch above their weight in seventh.

Ipswich have no teenagers assigned Transfermarkt values, leaving them bottom of the rankings, while Newcastle and Everton also stand out in the lower half of the rankings with teen values of only £9.9m and £10.5m respectively.

Spurs have the lowest teenage value of the traditional big six clubs, their total value of £23.1m putting them 11th.

Ayyoub Bouaddi , signed from Lille in August, accounts for over half of Manchester City's total, with a Transfermarkt value of £68.6m.

The 18-year-old midfielder sits alongside Chelsea winger Estevao as the most valuable teenager in the Premier League.

The next-most valuable teenager is centre-back Luka Vuskovic , who joined Brighton from Spurs for £50m in the summer and is valued by Transfermarkt at £51.4m.

Arsenal's total teen value is spread wider than their rivals'. In Myles Lewis-Skelly , Ethan Nwaneri and Max Dowman , who are valued at £38.6m, £30m and 25.7m respectively, the Gunners have three players among the 10 most valuable teenagers.

Dowman, who became the Premier League's youngest goalscorer aged 16 years and 73 days last season, is the only 16-year-old at any Premier League club with a Transfermarkt valuation.

Liverpool's 18-year-old winger Rio Ngumoha also features among the top 10, with the same Transfermarkt value as Dowman at £25.7m, along with Manchester United's Ayden Heaven , 19, and Aston Vila's Ibrahim Mbaye , 18.

The only five other teenagers with Transfermarkt v alues of over £20m are Brighton's Charalampos Kostoulas , Fulham's Josh King , Hull's Christos Mouzakitis , Liverpool's Giovanni Leoni and Sunderland's Chris Rigg .

Bouaddi and Estevao account for over half of Manchester City and Chelsea's total teenage values having been signed from Lille and Palmeiras at considerable expense, but Arsenal seemingly have an edge when it comes to generating value from their academy.

In addition to Lewis-Skelly, Dowman and the on-loan Nwaneri, all of whom are graduates of the club's Hale End youth system, the Gunners have 17-year-old defender Marli Salmon.

Like Dowman, Salmon impressed against Ipswich on Tuesday. His Transfermarkt value of £4.3m makes him the third-most valuable 17-year-old in the Premier League behind only Manchester City's Jeremy Monga and Aston Villa's Brian Madjo, both of whom were signed from other clubs in the summer.

Among the Premier League's 20 most valuable teenagers, according to Transfermarkt , the only players beyond Lewis-Skelly, Nwaneri and Dowman who came through the youth ranks at their current clubs are Fulham's King, Sunderland's Rigg and Tottenham winger Mikey Moore, who is on loan at Koln.

Heaven, who joined Manchester United from Arsenal last year, is another graduate of Hale End, further underlining the strength of the Gunners' production line.

Speaking on Sky Sports News, Paul Merson highlighted the importance of patience, specifically in the cases of Arsenal's Dowman and Manchester United's Gabriel.

"He's going past players like they're not there, like he's playing in his own age group," Merson said on Dowman.

"The first goal on Tuesday, the way he throws the dummy, leaves the defender on his backside and scores. It's just unbelievable.

"He's at an unbelievable Rolls Royce of a football club. He's got 15 years at least at the top. He's just got to be patient and that's hard because he'll think that he should be playing in the team now."

On Gabriel, Merson added: "First of all, he's an unbelievable talent. This kid can play as well. The problem now is with the lad and probably his agents and his family. I don't know him, so I'm only thinking from the outside.

"When you're watching Max Dowman and Rio Ngumoha getting given a chance at Liverpool and doing very well, he's probably thinking, I should be playing at Man United now as well.

"This is the problem you're going to have with the kids now of this day and age. They're so talented that they want to play straight away. When I was playing, it was unheard of at 16."

articles.title: Xabi Alonso: Chelsea manager says Blues needed 'an update' rather than a reset when he took over at Stamford Bridge
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports, Xabi Alonso discusses Chelsea's summer "update", why he's not looking for perfection, when to judge his Blues side and more; watch Chelsea vs Brentford live on Sky Sports Premier League from 7pm on Friday; kick-off 8pm
articles.body:
The 44-year-old signed a four-year contract in May and took over a Blues side that finished 10th in the Premier League, after parting ways with both Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior during a tumultuous campaign at Stamford Bridge.

That meant missing out on European football for the third time in four seasons.

"Not a reset - it was an update, I would say. To change or to take decisions in another direction," he said in an exclusive interview with Sky Sports .

"My main concern is the squad, the team, the players that we have, in which stage of their career they are, in which moments we want to bring them, what we have, what we can improve.

"Those were, for me, the important decisions, the important things to analyse before coming here. Once we agreed we wanted to take one direction, it was about taking decisions.

"Some of them we took, others will have to be taken, but we are convinced with all of them.

"Now it's competition time. It's not about improving, now it's with the team that we have to work hard, improve, knowing that we have to learn from mistakes, from the good things as well, and we are in that moment."

Alonso has taken charge of six games in all competitions so far; two wins, one draw and a defeat in the league and two wins from two in the Carabao Cup.

Next up, his Chelsea side make the short trip to the Gtech Community Stadium to take on Brentford in a west London derby on Friday night, which is live on Sky Sports .

"If I look for perfection, I will be frustrated always," he said.

"What I'm looking for is to reach a good level, good continuity, good solidity; to be a team that knows what they're going to do and have this confidence and this conviction whenever you are facing any opposition.

"We are in the process. We will get there when some processes are quicker or longer, but we are working to have that feeling and when you see that we are going on the pitch we have that belief that we know what we are going to do.

"The early days are just for games and I'm not that focused about the other teams. I'm very focused about my own team and all my players and the development that we will do, the process and the improvement that we have to make.

"We need to learn quick because the competition is furious in the Premier League and I'm sure that the Chelsea of the first day and the Chelsea of the last day in the Premier League will be different and I'm sure that it will be better. It will be getting better and better with weeks and with games."

Asked when people should just his team, he added: "It's not for me to answer.

"I prefer not to ask things from people. I prefer to do things.

"And knowing that, I am aware everything takes time in football, but time will tell."

Alonso: Joao Pedro could feature for Chelsea vs Brentford

Alonso has said Joao Pedro could feature against Brentford on Friday Night Football - despite pulling out of the Brazil squad with injury.

it was announced on Wednesday night that Pedro has withdrawn from the Brazil squad - raising concerns about his fitness levels as Chelsea look to get back to winning ways.

"In terms of injuries and in terms of the squad, we are having the last training session [on Friday]," Alonso said.

"No one is ruled out. I remain cautious and we wait. We will see [on Friday] if he's ready to play. We will take a decision."

Asked what he can say about Pedro's injury issues, Alonso simply replied: "No."

Asked if he could play against Brentford on Friday, but then not play for Brazil, Alonso said: "It is a possibility."

Then asked if Pedro is disappointed to be missing out of Brazil, especially given he was not selected for the World Cup, Alonso replied: "He has moved on from the summer, he has moved on from the World Cup.

"He has shown this desire, determination to have a great season so far. The summer is far away now.

"He will be [in the Brazil squad] in the future. I'm pretty sure he is going to be."

articles.title: Brentford 3-0 Chelsea: Defensive issues for Xabi Alonso laid bare after chastening west London derby defeat
articles.summary: Chelsea well beaten 3-0 by Brentford after dismal second half in the west London derby; Xabi Alonso's side continue to fail to keep clean sheets, concede from set-pieces and lack 'competitive mentality' when they fall behind; Chelsea now winless in three league games after a good start
articles.body:
Another defeat, their 11th of the calendar year - more than they had in 2025, with three months of this year to go. At least two goals conceded for the fifth straight Premier League game under Alonso. More set-piece woe.

"We dropped our consistency, our competitive mentality needed in the second half," said Alonso. That will concern Chelsea fans the most. It was way too easy for Brentford to take over that second half.

And there's another continuing trend: Chelsea being outbattled in a match. Remember, they were outrun in the vast majority of their Premier League matches last season.

The first thing you think about when you come up against Brentford is set pieces. Long throws, smart corners - the lot. And just like against Hull in their previous game, Chelsea lost control of the match by conceding once again from a set-piece.

This was the fourth goal they have conceded from a set-piece in five Premier League games - taking their overall tally since the start of last season to 23, the joint-worst out of any Premier League side.

Once again, the ball was put right on top of Emiliano Martinez towards the back post and neither the goalkeeper nor the outfield players were able to react. And the worst part of it for Chelsea? Brentford saw it coming a mile off.

"We did target [the back post] at half-time," said Vitaly Janelt to Sky Sports. "There was a big gap at the far post. We targeted that and I think it was our first corner of the second half."

And Chelsea are suffering from all these set-piece woes despite now having the best dead-ball coach in the league in Austin MacPhee. Bernardo Cueva, who was their set-piece coach before MacPhee and now has a different role at the club, was even pinched from Brentford by the Blues.

"We have not been good enough, at times we have been bullied and we need to improve at that," said Levi Colwill to Sky.

"But we trust in our set-piece coach; we are still adjusting to new things, but we do need to improve as a team."

It is not the only area where Chelsea need to improve defensively. The way they allow teams to penetrate their defensive third is among the worst in the division - they have gone 22 straight Premier League games without a clean sheet.

On average, Chelsea concede 2.2 non-penalty goals per game. And they deserve to, because the xG numbers say they are expected to allow that same number of shots on target on their goal.

What doesn't help is a clear inability to protect the penalty area. Chelsea are also in the top three this season for conceding shots in their own penalty area on average, allowing around 10 per game. Their goalkeepers get used as a battering ram.

With defensive numbers like these, it's no wonder Chelsea have been unable to hold onto a lead in their last three league games.

They explode out of the blocks so quickly - this was the first Premier League game where they failed to take the lead in the opening 10 minutes of the game, but they nearly did when Pedro Neto had a good chance saved.

And then when Chelsea fall behind, they have been pegged back so many times that the bad habits kick in. "It's about everything. It's about the mentality, the football and the tactical things that we need to keep improving," said Alonso.

"We concede the first goal, you're still in the game but then we lose the shape. We were out of control."

That control could be eased in the future when Moises Caicedo returns, but the lack of solidity they have without the Ecuadorian is a concern.

Two summer recruits in Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco started the Brentford game, but it was the Bees who looked stronger in midfield.

Keith Andrews' side arguably have the better squad depth in that area of the pitch as well - they won the match 3-0 with record signing Mamadou Sangare sat on the bench for over an hour.

Right now, Joao Pedro looks like Chelsea's most influential player from a goalscoring perspective. The 'JP Morgan' frontline was broken up for the first time this season - and Chelsea failed to score for the first time this season.

Of course, it was always going to take time for Alonso to implement his ideas at Stamford Bridge. This was a Chelsea team with seven summer signings in its starting line-up, with the Spaniard the fourth manager to take charge of the club in nine months.

"It doesn't happen overnight," former Chelsea captain Gary Cahill told Sky Sports. "I think with what you're saying he will be judged in the next five, six, seven weeks to get this right because you will have that time on the training ground and then we should start to see his methods coming through because we've seen him in an attacking sense."

"It's not just set-pieces," said Alonso on where Chelsea have to improve. "In defensive duels, build-up and controlling games." That being said, there aren't many more parts of the game besides those four.

"We've got a lot to work on over the international break," added Colwill. He can say that again.

articles.title: Celtic 0-1 Rangers: Neil Lennon calls for Hoops 'reset' but Martin O'Neill insists latest Old Firm defeat 'no disaster'
articles.summary: Rangers beat Celtic 1-0 to cut the gap at the top of the Scottish Premiership to two points; it was their second Old Firm win inside a week; Martin O'Neill's side have suffered three straight defeats
articles.body:
There was also the Hoops' defeat to Ferencvaros in the Europa League as they limped into the international break just two points clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership, as rampant Rangers showed they are ready to really challenge this season with a 1-0 victory at Parkhead .

It is a break that ex-Hoops boss Neil Lennon believes comes at the right time for the team to "reset". But, while O'Neill agrees with his former midfielder, he told Sky Sports their winless week is not a "disaster".

"It was a tough game. I don't think there's very much between the teams," the 74-year-old said.

"We should have created more. We had a lot of possession.

"It has been a tough week. The history of the club proves it will fight back from these things.

"It's concerning. Is it a disaster? I don't think so. We have to rethink and reset.

'All the best players were in a blue shirt'

"Outworked, which is the worst thing you can label at a team. Battered, actually battered."

Lennon, who had more than his share of Old Firm victories as a Celtic player and manager, did not hold back after watching Rangers run riot at Parkhead.

"Rangers were the far superior team, not just in physical attributes and running power, but football," he added.

"They played all the football. I thought Celtic were a lot better than they have been in the first half, without being brilliant. But second half, totally disjointed, totally outplayed.

"All the best players were in a blue shirt today. Celtic have a lot to ponder and a lot to work out.

"They've got an international break, which is probably coming at a good time for them.

"I know a lot of them may be away playing for their countries, but there needs to be a total reset because the last three performances in the space of a week have been very, very poor.

"Celtic have got big problems. They were smashed by Rangers and that's a concern," added Lennon's former Celtic team-mate Chris Sutton .

"Knowing Martin, he'll be greatly concerned.

"I don't like to disagree with him but it wasn't a close game. There was a massive gulf between the teams.

"I can't actually remember a Celtic team getting such a doing at Celtic Park from a Rangers team, which happened today.

"It looked like Celtic were making it up as they went along.

"Rangers were better in every department."

"It was men against boys, it was the exact same as last week."

Sky Sports' Kris Boyd was glowing in his analysis of his former team Rangers as he highlighted the growing problems for the current champions.

"To come and dominate a Celtic team as much as what they did, it should have been more convincing than what it was," he said.

"Celtic are lucky to get out of here 1-0. You look at the changes that Martin made at the start of the game, the subs that came on made zero impact as well.

"Right now, Celtic are a team that's in big trouble."

articles.title: Luke Littler's hopes of 2026 PDC major clean sweep over after defeat to Jonny Clayton at World Series of Darts Finals
articles.summary: Luke Littler has won World Championship, World Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay this year but World Series of Darts Finals trophy eluded him after quarter-final defeat; watch Littler's World Grand Prix defence live on Sky Sports from September 28
articles.body:
The world No 1 had won the first six premier events of the season after following his World Championship triumph at Alexandra Palace in January with the World Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

Littler was hoping to add the World Series of Darts Finals, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals trophies to complete a historic monopoly over the year - but ran into an inspired Clayton, who reeled off seven of the last eight legs to beat the teenager in a tournament ultimately won by Ross Smith .

Littler can still sweep the ranking events in 2026 - the World Series Finals, like the World Cup and Premier League, is non-ranked - if he wins the remaining four majors in Leicester, Dortmund, Wolverhampton and Minehead this autumn.

'The Nuke' has work to do to reach the Players Championship Finals, though, as he sits 125th on the Order of Merit in that series with six events of the regular season remaining and only the top 64 players advance to the finale in Somerset from November 27-29.

The teenager - currently £16,750 adrift of the final qualification spot - had hinted he may not try to reach the Players Championship Finals should his hopes of a major sweep end in the Netherlands.

The next Players Championship events are in Den Bosch on Tuesday and Wednesday before two more at the same venue on October 28 and 29 and then a final two in Leicester on November 4 and 5.

Jonny Clayton, speaking to ITV4 after victory over Luke Littler:

"To be honest, I just thought, 'relax, go out and try your best'.

"Luke wasn't at full flow. He missed a lot of darts at doubles, and that's the name of the game. You have to take your chances.

"All respect to Luke, he's fantastic but he gave me chances upon chances. That's not the Littler we all know. But Jonny Clayton can play darts as well!"

'Everyone is fallible - Littler felt the pressure'

Multi-time world champion Raymond van Barneveld, speaking to ITV4:

"It's the pressure. Everyone talks about: 'can Littler do the whole year and win all the big majors'. It gives big pressure.

"He wants to perform. He's the best player at the moment, but everyone is fallible. Everyone wants your scalp."

Littler, Humphries and Van Gerwen fall early

Victory at the World Series of Darts Finals would have been Littler's second in three years, having beaten Michael Smith to triumph in 2024 before losing to Michael van Gerwen in the final 12 months ago.

Littler had suffered scares earlier this week, rallying from 3-1 down to defeat Danny Noppert 6-4 in round one and then surviving a last-leg shoot-out versus Nathan Aspinall to win 10-9 in the last 16.

World No 2 Luke Humphries was eliminated by Dirk van Duijvenbode in round two on Saturday, while defending champion Van Gerwen fell in the opening round on Thursday, losing to Daryl Gurney.

Van Gerwen's World Series Finals victory last season is the only major he has won since 2023 and he has failed to reach an individual quarter-final in this year's majors.

The 37-year-old did make it to the final of the World Cup of Darts for Netherlands alongside doubles partner Van Veen, where the Dutch duo were beaten by England's Littler and Humphries.

That World Cup victory for Littler in Frankfurt in June means the European Championship is the only major title absent from his CV - something he will hope to rectify in Dortmund next month.

articles.title: Gary Neville: Michael Carrick has got to stop defending Man Utd players after lacklustre draw at Fulham
articles.summary: Man Utd came from behind to draw 1-1 at Fulham on Super Sunday; Lisandro Martinez scored an own goal before Matheus Cuhna equalised; however, the team's performance was once again called into question, with Gary Neville saying the team were a 'genuine disgrace'
articles.body:
While on Sky Sports co-commentary, Neville described their start to the second half at Craven Cottage as "the worst 15 minutes I have ever seen Manchester United play".

In that time, Carrick's side conceded a horror own goal from Lisandro Martinez, before Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike avoided a third straight league defeat.

The 1-1 draw followed losses to Manchester City last Sunday and a capitulation in the Carabao Cup third round against Brighton while there was a lack of urgency and energy at times from Man Utd in west London although Carrick dismissed the idea that his side were "passive".

Neville said: "I've never seen a Man Utd team walk out of possession as much as that. Michael has just said there was nothing wrong with the team's energy.

"Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he's defending them; he's loyal, he wants his players to work for him, and obviously there's a long way to go in the season.

"Both teams were the same. I called them mannequins. I've never seen a United team walk around as much as that. No alertness, no aliveness. No 'on your toes'. You should always be on your toes.

"Always shifting up two or three yards. They were just walking when Fulham were in possession. Fulham had 46 passes in the first couple of minutes to get their first shot.

"I don't know how many over-10-pass sequences Fulham had in that game, but the international break has come at a great time. There needs to be a rebalance.

"Very rarely do I say a team doesn't work hard or is lacking in effort. That's the ultimate criticism you can give a group of players.

"I'm always very careful to say that, but in those first 15 minutes of that second half, Man Utd and generally for the first 60 minutes, were a genuine disgrace. Nowhere near good enough without the ball.

"Michael is of course saying something different to us than he is saying privately. That would've really worried me. People will ask questions about him, but he knew that when he took the job.

"But there's no panic in that sense - no one is putting pressure on Carrick - but if those types of performances continue, he will find himself in a lot of trouble. They've got to work harder than that for him."

Neville also elaborated on how United's personnel is causing Carrick a headache. He said: "I wish he could play all of those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

"It's not just the defence and the back four that are causing him a problem - Mbeumo and Rashford are too high and wide. They don't narrow back in. You've got Tielmans and Mainoo in midfield who are a little bit one-paced. Baleba will probably come in there. Bruno floats around a little bit, and then Cunha floats around a little bit.

"You've got these five or six players who are better with the ball than without the ball.

"It would be great to see them score loads of goals and maybe concede one or two and go and win games, but there is going to have to be a reset from the point of view of defensive structure because there are far too many of them walking on the pitch."

Cunha: They put in more energy than us - we cannot accept this

Cunha also said Man Utd lacked energy at Craven Cottage, telling Sky Sports : "It is frustrating for us. After the goal, we played much better and had a lot of character. It needs to be from the start. It is only one point but we should never play for one point.

"It is hard. They put in more energy than us, we cannot accept this. We need to do our best. We need to improve in every single position. It is only the beginning. Last season was the same, with noise around, but we finished third."

However, Carrick did not subscribe to the same view, adding to Sky Sports: "I didn't think we did [look passive]. Did you think we were passive? Football is a difficult game.

"We controlled a lot of the first half and we played a lot of good football today. There is going to be spells when you don't have it go your own way.

"The goal they scored, and arguably there is a foul at one point on Matheus [Cunha], and it is two deflections. It goes their way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don't think anyone gets that in this league."

articles.title: Man City serve up pure chaos under Enzo Maresca as Cody Gakpo shines for Liverpool - Premier League hits and misses
articles.summary: Sky Sports' football writers dissect the action from a thrilling Super Sunday in the Premier League as Sunderland's visit to Manchester City contained an astonishing eight goals and Cody Gakpo proved his importance to Liverpool at Bournemouth
articles.body:
Man City's captivating but chaotic 5-3 win over Sunderland could not have been further removed from the picture of control so often associated with City under Pep Guardiola. "We want to control but the other team don't want to allow us," Enzo Maresca reflected.

Sunderland made command of the game very difficult, but City equally did themselves no favours.

Maresca had warned of the size of the task pre-match - and so it proved. "I knew how good they are, off the ball very aggressive," he added, after the Black Cats terrorised the Etihad. Rarely have City conceded so much territory or given up so many chances at home, nor do they often ship three goals.

Brian Brobbey served up another masterclass in hold-up play, just as he did against Arsenal last week. Except on this occasion he matched his physical presence with three excellent goals. Every time Brobbey won his duel against Ruben Dias - which was often - there was space to play off.

He was joined in waves of attack by Enzo Le Fee, before Nilson Angulo and Thomas Meunier swiftly arrived from wide. Suddenly City were overloaded. And it happened time after time. Neither Elliot Anderson nor Enzo Fernandez could get to grips with the physical battle, unable to cope when Sunderland pressed man to man or played longer.

City were out-duelled by a substantial amount, outrun too. Brobbey won 10 of the 12 duels he contested and drew a game-high five fouls. He could not be shackled, a clear winner of the tug-of-war.

But fortunately for Maresca, City were able to play Sunderland at their own game for enough of the match to score five times themselves. They picked on mistakes, digging deep to get the job done the anti-Pep way. Imperfect but effective.

Perhaps that should count for something, too. Laura Hunter

Michael Carrick is getting a reputation for the way he calmly bats away criticism of his Man Utd team, contrasting with the noise of those detractors. He has had to do that more and more in the past week, with a Manchester derby loss followed by a Carabao Cup collapse, and now a scrambled point at previously bottom-club Fulham. At Craven Cottage he was asked about United's joint-worst start to a Premier League season and pointed to fine margins. The 25-yard stunner at Everton, the incorrectly awarded City goal, the bizarre own goal at Fulham and two strikes against posts earlier in the game. He has a point.

But the problem is the accumulation of poor performances is starting to add up. As Carrick would say, it's not been all bad in any game but the positives are being outweighed by United's shortcomings. Physically, defensively, and in possession United have been found wanting in key moments and keep paying the price.

A 10-point gap has already yawned open to table-topping City and the prospect of United improving on last season's third place seems unrealistic right now. "It's still a big season ahead," Carrick defiantly told the press on Sunday evening. But a big shift, encompassing more than just finer details in a game, is required if it's to be a successful one. Peter Smith

In every single Liverpool game he has started this season, Cody Gakpo has produced a golden moment in front of goal.

A goal at Newcastle on the opening weekend, a silky assist against Nottingham Forest, assists for both goals in the win over Ipswich, another one and a goal against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup - but this intervention in the 1-0 win at Bournemouth was the best of the lot.

Latest news and rumours: Bournemouth | Liverpool

With Liverpool struggling for attacking influence, Gakpo's hard-fought run and cross down the right wing was vital in the build-up to Alexader Isak's winner. "The difficult part of the goal is from him," said Iraola about Gakpo, who is unfortunate not to be accredited with the assist.

But Gakpo also starred defensively at Bournemouth, winning more duels than any other player on the pitch. He shut down one of the Cherries' biggest threats. "I know Adrien Truffert very well and he demands a lot from you defensively. Cody has been very important in both ways," added Iraola.

When Gakpo is absent, Liverpool are not the same team - as seen in the goalless draw with Fulham where the Dutchman was only fit enough for the bench.

Looking at this form, it is absolutely staggering that Liverpool considered sanctioning the sale of Gakpo this summer. Where would they be without him? Sam Blitz

From the highs of their first win in Europe against Real Sociedad on Thursday to the lows of yet another defeat in the Premier League.

Bournemouth now go into the three-week international break without a win. A sour note to leave on given the joy that followed from their victory in San Sebastian.

Neither side impressed at the Vitality Stadium and for the most part, the Cherries looked the more likely team to go on and snatch three points.

But with Justin Kluivert sidelined through injury and no other changes made from the team in midweek, they just did not have the legs to go one step further in front of goal.

Marco Rose has made just two changes to their Premier League starting XIs this season, the fewest of any side.

That is not sustainable while balancing European football. Rotation is needed to keep this squad fit; otherwise they risk slipping into an unwanted relegation battle this season. Patrick Rowe

Alvaro Arbeloa says Fulham are improving and it is a fair assessment after draws against Liverpool and Man Utd at the end of a testing start in the Premier League.

A third consecutive defeat in early September at home to Crystal Palace heightened concerns Fulham may be in a relegation fight after four trouble-free seasons under Marco Silva, but they have something to build on heading into the international break.

Josh King has been their brightest player across the first five games with two goals and is showing why he is so highly regarded by the club having come through the academy. David Affengruber, an £8.5m summer signing from Elche, shone on debut at centre-back against Liverpool and appears to have dislodged Joachim Andersen for now.

Gonzalo Garcia scored on the opening day of the season following his move from Real Madrid but has managed just two shots on target from 15 so far.

The next six weeks will be pivotal for Arbeloa. He has more time to work with his squad now ahead of fixtures against the three newly-promoted clubs when the season resumes. David Richardson

Crystal Palace arrived at Elland Road with 11 goals conceded from their opening four Premier League games. They left with a clean sheet and, on balance in the second half, will probably feel they could have taken all three points.

Latest news and rumours: Leeds | Crystal Palace

This was a spirited, disciplined performance from Palace. They came out after the break with a completely different mindset and put Leeds under pressure.

Leeds were strangely flat. Dominic Calvert-Lewin was starved of service for long periods and even when the chances did arrive, Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez was there to deny him.

In the end, 0-0 felt like a reflection of two sides who cancelled each other out, but Palace can take far more encouragement from this performance than Leeds can.

For Pierre Sage, though, this is the sort of defensive display he will hope can become the foundation of a turnaround. William Bitibiri
